lyrics:
The talaros, a woven openwork
Holds what’s thought true
Misconstrued as you
And what is not falls through
The weavers never meant to hold
Such weight upon the stakes
Nothing freely escapes
The account of our mistakes

Every choice a new example
Of the flame or just the candle

A tablet scored, a page impressed
A vivid description of what works best
All mostly meaningless
Not subject nor object nor truth disavowed
Unreasonably quiet and silently loud
Of woven edge and borrowed reeds
The talaros serves, then releases
Once holding on, then letting go
Of all the weight it gathers
Better still, to let them go
What’s holding and what’s held
The talaros never failed
You are not what it gathered

Every choice a new example
Of the flame or just the candle
A tablet scored, a page impressed
A vivid description of what works best

Unreasonably quiet and silently loud

style: Chill wave with ambient features and an odd, warped edge: hazy Juno-106 pads, detuned electric piano, tape-wobble synth arps, and a distant MIDI guitar line through chorus and plate reverb, Slow 78 BPM, half-time drum machine, soft sub-bass, granular textures, reverse tails, and unresolved minor-key harmonies suspended in a weightless mix

impression.text: The track features a lush, synthesizer-driven texture that blends nostalgia with a dreamlike, melancholic emotional atmosphere. It maintains a steady, moderate energy level propelled by a pulsing bassline and clean, gated drum sounds that give the rhythm a solid, danceable feel. The production is exceptionally polished and spacious, utilizing wide reverb on the vocals and clever panning to keep the dense synth pads from crowding the mix. A defining moment occurs during the transition into the chorus, where the soundscape expands dramatically to elevate the emotional impact of the soaring vocal melody.

review.review_text: The talaros of the title is a woven Greek strainer, and PCBender builds the whole song around that image: a vessel that holds what it can and lets the rest fall through. It's the kind of conceit that could collapse under its own cleverness, but the arrangement keeps it grounded and weightless at once, hazy Juno pads and a tape-wobbled arp drifting over a half-time pulse at a patient 103 BPM. The best moment is the lift into the chorus, where the mix opens up and the vocal climbs into "Not subject nor object nor truth disavowed / Unreasonably quiet and silently loud," a line that pays off both halves of its paradox. That the song hangs in A# major rather than resolving anywhere firm is the point: "Better still, to let them go," it decides, and the release lands. The lyric leans dense, and the third pass through the chorus asks for more patience than the first, but the payoff earns it. A highlight, and one that holds the room by staying quiet.
